summary: Inventory protocol-compatible new information sources for the under-cover block, measure their ceilings on a non-keyframe dev set, and synthesize an S1-E13 plan plus the protocol decisions for the user

maps.summary:
I sorted what could tell stage 1 how far an object extends beyond what c_ini shows, using the protocol rules in docs/muvod-protocol.md, docs/mvvos-algorithm-analysis.md §1 and docs/stage1-E8.md. Every new number is from the DEV set (20 non-keyframe frames × 2 non-c_ini annotated cameras × 17 scenes = 13,239 rows). No keyframe label map, cache or prediction was opened. Keyframe numbers below are quoted from existing files (extent_vis_report.txt, coupling3.txt, the E2 docs), not recomputed.

**What counts as beyond-c_ini on DEV.** I ported the S1-E11 visibility classes to numpy. The port gives identical class counts to the torch rows (train_vis.json) on all 6,608 overlapping DEV rows. On DEV, 47.7% of target GT is invisible from c_ini: outside 20.1%, occluded 20.1%, no depth 7.5% (all as shares of target GT). For the same 22 under-cover (scene, camera, object) on DEV frames it is 66.4%: outside 34.7%, occluded 17.1%, no depth 14.6%. The keyframe missed region, quoted from extent_vis_report.txt, is 1,325,193 px: visible from c_ini 0.091, outside 0.366, occluded 0.160, no depth 0.384.

**(i) Allowed under the protocol we adopted.** All exist for 17/17 scenes.
- **c_ini frame-0 mask (the input).** By definition it reaches only the visible class.
  - Reprojected onto its own GT, it covers 1.9% of the keyframe missed region.
  - 60.4% of DEV occluded pixels are hidden by the same object (c_ini sees that object along the ray); 49.4% for the 22 objects.
  - Splatting c_ini's labelled Pi3 points forward into the target reaches 14.8% of DEV no-depth pixels, but only 0.5% for the 22 objects and 0% for the Dog tree.
- **RGB of all rig cameras at the same instant** (9–46 per scene, 369 in total), plus Pi3 geometry derived from them. Points visible from at least one other camera: outside 0.888, occluded 0.931, no depth 0 (DEV); 0.682 of beyond-c_ini for the 22 objects. Applied to the keyframe class mix this gives 0.458–0.474, matching the 0.459 the E11 report measured on the keyframe. But those cameras carry no labels, and existing neighbour seeds cover only 0.189 of the keyframe missed region.
- **c_ini RGB at other times** (video). The protocol allows it, but it falls outside the single-instant stage-1 scope.
  - It cannot reach outside pixels: the rig is fixed (Pi3 relative rotation varies at most 0.67° across frames).
  - Occluded: 16.0% of DEV occluded pixels have a moving occluder. The cross-time visibility gain above the noise floor is 3.8% of occluded pixels on DEV and 0.0% for the 22 objects.
  - No depth: the same target pixel has valid depth at another frame for 10.9% (3.4% for the Dog tree).
- **SAM 3 visual exemplar from c_ini's box, and the target's own appearance.** These act on the target image, so in principle they reach every class including no-depth. The existing E2 exemplar-detection gate failed (9/19 pairs, hallucination on 129/132 empty rows).
- **Fold-trained priors** (other scenes' GT). Allowed with the training-data caveat from E8; E12 showed this route made the model more conservative.

**(ii) Separate track only.**
- **Label names as SAM 3 text prompts.** Source: Data/MVSeg/<s>/Mask/objects_labels.json, identical to stage1/Data/<s>/objects_labels.json; 17/17 scenes, 459 objects, 73 names, 11 of them merged names such as handrail_or_fence. No method uses these files today, only evaluation and diagnostics.
  - In principle the prompt reaches 100% of the beyond-c_ini region in every class, including no-depth.
  - Ambiguity: 297 of the 398 basic objects share their name with another object in the same scene.
  - Pixel-weighted, scene-unique names cover 79.4% of the DEV beyond-c_ini region and 97.9% for the 22 objects.
  - 13 of the 22 under-cover objects have a unique name, including all 9 env objects; all 50 env objects in the dataset have scene-unique names.
  - The same metadata names the 61 complete-only objects, which must not be prompted in the main track.
- **A second annotated reference camera B.** Every annotated camera is a scoring camera, so J&F³ itself would change.
  - Label transfer from B's GT reaches 17.7% of the DEV beyond-c_ini region (outside 0.130, occluded 0.290, no depth 0) and 7.8% for the 22 objects (outside 0.018).
  - On the keyframe (existing coupling3.txt), B's warped GT covers at least 50% of the missed pixels in 2/22 pairs and at most 3% in 11/22, including the Dog tree, both CBABasketball grandstands and the Welder ground.
- **Calibration from the source datasets** (models.json, poses_bounds.npy). Not in the MUVOD distribution or the repo, and gives no labels or depth.

**(iii) Forbidden.**
- Any annotated camera's GT as input: the scoring cameras at any frame, and c_ini at frames other than the reference frame (those 20 frames are scored).
- Per-camera object-presence sets.
- Training on the test scene.
- Choosing or tuning anything on the keyframe.

**Conclusion.** For the under-cover region, nothing within (i) carries labels into the outside and no-depth classes. The geometric sources give zero reach on no-depth, and the label-carrying ones barely reach the outside class. The only sources that reach all three classes in principle act on the target image: label names (ii) and exemplars or appearance (i). Name ambiguity is small on exactly the objects that fail.

implications: Within the adopted protocol (i), no source carries labels into the outside and no-depth classes. The c_ini mask, its forward splat, c_ini video frames and B do not reach the outside class. Geometric transfer cannot reach no-depth by construction. That leaves 0.75 of the keyframe missed region (outside 0.366 + no-depth 0.384) for target-image-based sources only.

Other rig cameras see 0.888 of DEV outside and 0.931 of DEV occluded pixels, matching the keyframe 0.459 when projected. So the gap is labels, not visibility: any (i) design must create labels in non-annotated views without them all descending from the one c_ini memory. E11 already measured that today's neighbour seeds cover only 0.189 of the keyframe missed region.

c_ini RGB at later frames is effectively worthless for the under-cover block. It gets 0 on outside (fixed rig), 0.000 net gain on occluded for the 22 objects and 0.034 on the Dog tree's no-depth pixels. It would also break single-instant stage-1 scope, so it is not worth pursuing.

A second annotated reference camera (ii) is weak exactly where it is needed. It reaches 0.078 of the beyond-c_ini region for the 22 objects (outside 0.018) and at most 3% of missed pixels on the four costliest keyframe pairs (quoted). It also changes J&F³ because every annotated camera is scored. Not recommended.

Label-name text prompts (ii) are the only listed source that in principle reaches all three classes, Dog-tree no-depth included. They are nearly unambiguous on the failing objects (97.9% of their beyond-c_ini pixels have scene-unique names; all env objects are unique) but ambiguous in general (297/398 basic objects share a name). Any experiment must be reported as a separate track, split the merged '_or_' names, and never prompt the 61 complete-only objects in the main track.

The (i)-legal counterpart of the text prompt is a SAM 3 visual exemplar from c_ini's box. It has the same in-principle reach, but the existing E2 gate failed (keyframe, pre-rule), mostly on hallucination. Measuring exemplar or text precision on large env objects (wall, ground, grandstand, tree) needs a DEV GPU run; that is not done here.

In the occluded class, 49–60% of pixels are hidden by the same object, so the reference input already labels that ray. That is decode/geometry-tolerance territory (input already available), not new information, and E11 already found decode-only changes do not move the 22 pairs.

Caveat: forward-splat and multi-view reach are computed at Pi3 work resolution and nearest-upsampled. The cross-time test relies on per-frame Pi3 runs aligned by median depth ratio, so its noise floor (0.028–0.162) is reported next to the signal.

maps.summary:
I probed the frozen SAM 3 package (SCSam3/sam3/sam3; the scsam3 image's /opt/sam3/sam3 is byte-identical by `diff -rq`, excluding __pycache__) and sorted its single-image, no-memory prompting modes. Everything ran in scsam3 with the cached facebook/sam3 checkpoint (SCSam3/hf_cache snapshot 3c879f39, sam3.pt), offline, with strict state-dict loading and no missing-key or warning lines in the logs. A single `methods/sam3_single.load_model()` (build_scsam3_video_model) serves every mode: the detector (model.detector, a Sam3ImageOnVideoMultiGPU) and the tracker (model.tracker, an SCSam3TrackerPredictor) live in the same checkpoint.

The probe ran on three DEV frames (t=10; ref_frame is 0 in all three scenes and the script asserts t != ref_frame): Dog camera_0004, Welder camera_0004 and Carpark v0. No keyframe was touched and nothing was tuned. The task asked for one frame. I added Welder and Carpark because Dog's Pi3 geometry turned out to be degenerate, which made the mask-prompt question unanswerable on Dog alone.

**Supported modes and exact call paths:**

1. **Point and box prompts through the tracker used as an image model** (the existing repo path). `methods/sam3_single.segment()` calls `model.init_state([frame])`, then `SCSam3VideoInference.add_tracker_new_points` (SCSam3VideoInference.py:1425). That runs `_prepare_backbone_feats` (a full backbone pass plus a detector grounding pass), then `SCSam3TrackerPredictor.add_new_points`, then `Sam3TrackerBase._forward_sam_heads` on an initial-conditioning frame with `no_mem_embed`. Labels are 1/0 for points and 2/3 for box corners. It returns a bool [H,W] mask.

2. **The SAM-1-task interactive predictor**, `sam1_task_predictor.SAM3InteractiveImagePredictor.predict(point_coords, point_labels, box, mask_input, multimask_output)`. It returns masks [C,H,W] with C=3 or 1, predicted IoUs [C], and low-res logits [C,288,288]. Upstream wires it through `build_sam3_image_model(enable_inst_interactivity=True)` + `Sam3Processor.set_image` + `Sam3Image.predict_inst` (sam3_image.py:596); nothing in this repo uses that route. My probe wraps `model.tracker` (the same tracker.* weights) and builds its features exactly as `predict_inst` does: the detector backbone's sam2 neck, then `sam_mask_decoder.conv_s0/conv_s1`, `_prepare_backbone_features` and `+ no_mem_embed`. Its point masks agree with path 1 at IoU 0.89–0.97.

3. **Dense mask prompts**, which exist in two forms:
   - (a) `predict(mask_input=[1,288,288])` sends the mask through the SAM prompt encoder's `mask_downscaling` as a dense embedding, so it really goes through the decoder.
   - (b) The tracker's `add_tracker_new_mask` (SCSam3VideoInference.py:1677) → `SCSam3TrackerPredictor.add_new_mask` (:360) → `_use_mask_as_output` (sam3_tracker_base.py:388) is a pass-through. The output equals the input (IoU vs input 1.000 for all 28 objects tested across the three frames); the decoder only makes the object pointer and memory.

4. **Text (concept) prompts to the detector.** `Sam3Processor(model.detector).set_image(PIL)` then `.set_text_prompt(str)` calls `Sam3Image.forward_grounding`. The video-level equivalent is `SCSam3VideoInference.add_prompt(text_str=...)` (:848). Of 200 queries, those with sigmoid(logit)·presence > 0.5 are kept. It returns state['masks'] [N,1,H,W] bool, 'boxes' (xyxy pixels) and 'scores'.

5. **Image-exemplar boxes.** `Sam3Processor.add_geometric_prompt(box_cxcywh_norm, label)` works on the same image only. Every shipped API is same-image: the video `add_prompt` keeps the visual box only on its own frame via `per_frame_geometric_prompt`. There is no shipped cross-image API.
   - Cross-image still works without changing the package. Encode the box with `det.geometry_encoder` on the reference image's features, then put that token sequence after the text tokens in the target image's prompt — the same concatenation `Sam3Image._encode_prompt` does — and run `_run_encoder`, `_run_decoder` and `_run_segmentation_heads`.
   - Check: when the exemplar image is the target itself, this reproduces `add_geometric_prompt`'s logits exactly (max abs diff 0.0).
   - Caveat: the box token carries the reference image's box coordinates (direct projection and position encoding) as well as ROI-pooled features, and 3 encoder layers cross-attend the reference image.

6. **The detector takes no mask prompts** (`geometry_encoder.mask_encoder` is None). `Sam3Image.forward` ignores point prompts for concept segmentation, and `Sam3Processor` exposes only boxes.

7. **There is no automatic "everything" mode.** The package has no automatic mask generator. Generic text ('object', 'thing') returns 0 detections on all three frames. I emulated a SAM-1-style everything mode instead: a point grid through the interactive head, 3 masks per point, filters pred-IoU ≥ 0.8, stability ≥ 0.95 and object score > 0, then box NMS at 0.7.

**Can the interactive predictor take a dense mask from the reprojected reference GT?** Yes, mechanically. The reference GT of the same dev frame goes through `project_reference_masks(*reproj_inputs(Cache/pi3_frames/<t>, ...))`. It is fed either as ±10 logits at 288², or the tracker's own way: its learned `mask_downsample` conv applied at 1152². Either way:
- **Mask alone does nothing useful.** The output is about the projection, so the part not seen from c_ini is not recovered.
- **Mask plus the projection's bounding box is the only mask variant that adds recall.** On Carpark recall goes from 0.70 to 0.83 at precision 0.91, and IoU from 0.680 to 0.798.
- **The gain depends on how good the projection is.** Welder improves only from 0.364 to 0.436. On Dog camera_0004 the Pi3 geometry is broken: only 25.4 % of pixels are visible from c_ini, 50 % have valid depth, and the projected dog has precision 0.38. A host-side numpy re-check gave the same projection IoUs, and Dog t=5 behaves the same as t=10.

On repeated runs the outputs are deterministic: all 412 non-timing values were identical between two Dog runs.

Costs were measured on an RTX 6000 Ada, as the median of 3 CUDA-synchronised calls after one warm-up, with backbone features cached where noted:
- **Backbone:** about 70 ms per image.
- **Prompts:** a mask-prompt pass is 6–14 ms; a text prompt about 44 ms; an exemplar grounding about 30 ms.
- **sam3_single.segment:** about 120–130 ms per call, because each call reruns the backbone and the detector.
- **Everything-mode emulation:** 0.65 s for a 32×32 grid.
- **Model load and memory:** load takes 8.5 s warm (27 s cold); the whole probe peaked at 12.7 GB.

implications: A dense mask prompt cannot add the part of an object that c_ini does not see. Mask-only output stays at about the projection (Carpark 0.659 vs 0.680), and the tracker's add_new_mask is a pure pass-through. Mask plus the projection's bounding box adds recall only inside the box the projection already spans (Carpark recall 0.70 to 0.83), so it cannot reach the under-cover pixels outside c_ini's view.

The only single-image modes that can produce extent independent of the reference memory are the detector modes (text and exemplar boxes). The detector also handles large background regions far better than the SAM head: the same-image exemplar on Dog's tree gives 0.845 against 0.040 for an interactive box. Of the 22 failing under-cover pairs, 5 are such regions (env objects), Dog camera_0004's tree among them.

Text prompts need label names. Those come from annotation metadata, so whether text is a legal input under the MUVOD protocol has to be decided before any text-based arm is registered. Text also returns instance sets (Carpark 'car', Dog 'tree' with 15 instances), so it would need a selection or merge rule, for example overlap with the current seed or the projection.

Cross-image exemplars are feasible without touching the frozen package, verified with an exact-logit sanity check. They work on the small-baseline pinhole rig (Carpark top-instance 0.793) but fail on the hemisphere rig (Dog 0.157). A likely cause is that the box token also encodes the reference image's box position. Adding label text helps when the object is a large region (Dog sky 0.015 to 0.923) but can pick the wrong instance (Carpark top-score 0.793 to 0.609).

Projection-derived prompts depend entirely on Pi3 quality. Dog's Pi3 cache is degenerate (25 % of pixels visible from c_ini, projected dog precision 0.38), so prompts built from reprojection fail there regardless of the prompt mode. Dog was the motivating under-cover case.

Cost is not a constraint. Any of these modes adds roughly 70 ms of backbone per view plus tens of ms per prompt. Calling sam3_single.segment per object wastes about 50–60 ms per call on the repeated backbone and detector pass; computing features once and reusing them avoids that.
SAM 3 has no everything mode. The point-grid emulation misses most large regions (mean best IoU 0.26–0.37), so it is a poor source of candidate extents.

I built a DEV set and a scratch decode route for the adopted stage-1 preset geoset_rep_x (arm geoset_pred_ft, --gate reproj --xcl out, the held-out fold checkpoint). The keyframe was never decoded or scored, and no tracked file changed; git status is the same as at the start.

DEV set (fixed before any decode):
- 17 scenes. For each scene, the train frames other than the ref frame, every 4th (index [3::4]), which gives t = ref+4, +8, +12, +16, +20: 85 frames.
- Cameras: the 2 annotated non-reference cameras (meta mask_cams minus ref_cam).
- Reference: c_ini = meta ref_cam at frame t. Reference mask = c_ini GT at t, restricted to the scene's basic object set (docs/raw/muvod_object_sets.json seed_ids_c_ini).
- A pair is (scene, t, cam, obj) with obj present in c_ini at t and GT non-empty in cam. This is the same gt_px > 0 rule as the 664 keyframe pairs.

Can decode_scene run on frame t? Yes, unchanged. Only one thing ties it to the keyframe: `cache = cache_dir(data, scene, "pi3")`. Before relying on that, I diffed the inputs. For all 17 scenes, the root images/ and masks/ and Cache/pi3 are byte-identical to frames/<ref>/ and Cache/pi3_frames/<ref>. So pointing at frame t uses the same code path. Every dev frame has images, Pi3 caches with a MANIFEST for all cameras, and GT for the 3 annotated cameras. Backbone caches are not needed, because decode_scene computes features live.

The wrapper is stage1/geomem/runs/_e13_dev-route/dev_decode.py, with three changes around an unmodified decode_scene:
1. Scene: `common.load_scene(data, scene, frame=t)`, with the c_ini label map restricted to the basic set.
2. Pi3: `run.cache_dir` is patched to Cache/pi3_frames/<t>.
3. Cameras: scene.cams is restricted to {c_ini} + the 2 eval cameras + the k=3 nearest candidates of each (from the frame's own Pi3 centres).

On the first dev frame of every scene, the restricted decode gave the same eval-camera masks, byte for byte, as a full all-camera decode (17/17 frames). Each decode loads the scene's own-fold checkpoint, and the leak guard (stage1.check_preflight) passes.

Results on the DEV set: mean J&F 0.9078 over 3300 pairs. Under the task's definition, 140 pairs (49 distinct scene/cam/object) are under-cover. 95.2 % of their missed pixels (pixel-weighted) are not visible from c_ini, and the round-1 masks of the 3 nearest cameras cover only 8.3 % of them. This matches the keyframe anatomy already on record (91 % invisible, 19 % neighbour cover), so the dev set reproduces the failure.

Any decode-side candidate can reuse dev_decode.py by changing PRESET or args, at about 11 min for all 85 frames, and be scored with dev_score.py --masks <root> in the same layout without touching the keyframe.

Under-cover failures on the dev set look the same as on the keyframe: 95 % of the missed pixels are invisible to c_ini (91 % without the Dog tree), and the nearest neighbours' round-1 masks cover only about 8 % of them. A design for 'new information' can therefore be built and measured on the dev set.

Pixel-weighted statistics are dominated by Dog camera_0004 tree (48 % of missed pixels, mostly no Pi3 depth) and by the FlameSteak cam01 wall (25 %, outside the c_ini image). Report pair-mean figures and the without-Dog variant next to the pixel-weighted ones.

The task's under-cover definition has no precision condition, so it also takes in 73 spill, miss and wrong-object pairs where the seed is on the wrong pixels as well. For a method aimed at under-coverage, use the clean subset (precision >= 0.85: 67 pairs, 24 objects) as the target. Report the full population as a side effect.

Dev pairs are near-replicates: 5 frames within 20 frames of the keyframe, the same objects, 49 distinct under-cover objects behind 140 pairs. Use scene- or object-cluster bootstrap CIs, not pair-level ones. A dev gain is evidence about the same scenes, not an independent test.

The k=3 neighbour sets come from each frame's own Pi3, so they change from frame to frame in 8 scenes (5 distinct sets over 5 frames in Dog, Welder and AlexaMeadeFacePaint). The dev decode is faithful to running the preset at frame t, but this is one source of difference between dev and keyframe behaviour.

If more dev statistics are needed, the full set of 20 non-reference frames would cost about 45 min of restricted decode, split into jobs under 20 min. dev_decode.py would need OFFSET/STRIDE changed, and it skips frames that already have a DONE marker.

measures.summary:
Candidate C does not work on the DEV set. Prompting SAM 3 (single image, no memory) with the part of the reference GT that reprojects visibly into each target view, then adding SAM's segment to the adopted dev mask under the add-only rules, lowers mean J&F over all 3300 dev pairs. The registered primary variant moves it from 0.90782 to 0.90660 (−0.00122, scene-cluster 95 % CI [−0.00263, +0.00018]). On the 140-pair dev under-cover population it gains +0.00557 [−0.00110, +0.01744]. That gain comes almost entirely from one object, the CBABasketball v06 billboard (5 pairs, +0.149 each). Without it the other 135 under-cover pairs gain +0.00027 [−0.00158, +0.00216].

Of the added pixels, 0.359 belong to the target object; 0.626 land on other seeded objects. SAM's segment touches only 3.8 % of the under-cover missed pixels at all, so no composition rule can recover more than that. No keyframe frame was decoded, prompted or scored, and no tracked file was changed (the only modified tracked file, MVSeed/runs/e4c_project.json, was already modified before this run).

**How it was run.** The design was written to REGISTRATION.txt before any proposal was computed.

*Per view.* For each dev view (85 non-keyframe frames × 2 annotated non-reference cameras = 170 views), I took c_ini's GT at frame t, restricted to the basic object set. I reprojected it with that frame's Pi3 cache using project_reference_masks (OCC_TOL 0.01), which gives P_o, the visible-from-c_ini part of each object, and the visibility mask. The target image's features were computed once per view, as Sam3Image.predict_inst does, and fed to SAM3InteractiveImagePredictor around model.tracker. Every object with |P_o| ≥ 20 px (3389 of 3952 seeded objects) was prompted with 5 registered variants:
- **pts (primary):** 3 interior points of P_o, 3 output masks, SAM's own choice by highest predicted IoU.
- **pts_whole:** the same call, keeping the largest of the 3 masks.
- **pts_neg:** the same points plus one negative point inside each other object's projection.
- **box:** the bounding box of P_o.
- **mask_box:** P_o as a dense mask through the tracker's learned downsampler, plus its box.

*Composition, applied to all seeded objects at once.* For object o with dev mask D_o and SAM segment S_o:
1. Candidate pixels C_o: in S_o, not visible from c_ini, outside D_o, and outside every other object's dev mask.
2. A_o: the C_o pixels in the 8-connected components of C_o ∪ D_o that contain a D_o pixel.
3. Pixels claimed by two or more objects are dropped.
4. New mask N_o = D_o ∪ A_o.

*Fixed constants:* MIN_PROJ_PX 20, no predicted-IoU gate, no growth cap.

*Scoring.* I scored with mvseg2d.metrics.jf_pair. The baseline J/F I recomputed equals dev_pairs.json exactly, on all 3300 pairs, with 0 class-count mismatches. I also wrote the primary's composed masks and re-scored them independently with the dev-route's dev_score.py in the container: the per-pair deltas match to 1.1e-16.

**Primary (pts | 20 | no gate):**
- **All 3300 pairs:** ΔJ&F −0.00122 (ΔJ −0.00156, ΔF −0.00088). 2535 pairs changed: 1448 up (sum +4.95), 1087 down (sum −8.98). Pairs that already had J&F ≥ 0.8 lose −5.36 in total.
- **Under-cover 140:** +0.00557 [−0.00110, +0.01744] (object-cluster bootstrap); 51 up, 32 down. 12 of the 140 had no prompt at all (|P_o| < 20); for example CBABasketball v06 grandstand has a 0-px projection.
- **Clean 67** (the under-cover pairs whose dev mask already has precision ≥ 0.85): +0.01225 [−0.00012, +0.03601].
- **The other 3160 pairs:** −0.00152 [−0.00284, −0.00027].
- **Added pixels:** 2,160,330 px; precision 0.359 pooled (0.533 pair-mean). By class: outside 0.284, occluded 0.461, no-depth 0.309. On the under-cover pairs the precision is 0.776, but 140,869 of the 161,152 added px there are the billboard.
- **Missed pixels recovered (under-cover):** 0.0226 (pair-mean 0.039). By class: outside 0.049, occluded 0.015, no-depth 0.0002. Dog camera_0004 tree 0.001; FlameSteak cam01 wall 0.002; CBABasketball v24 grandstand 0.002.

**Where the added pixels go.** MUVOD's GT labels essentially every pixel (label 0 is 6.5e-8 of pixels), so nothing lands on unlabelled background. The 64 % of added pixels that are wrong sit on other objects, nearly all of them seeded ones whose dev masks left those pixels unclaimed. By distance from the dev mask:
- within 3 px: 32 % of added pixels, precision 0.60
- 3 px up to the boundary tolerance: 30 %, precision 0.40
- beyond the tolerance (the "new extent" part): 37.5 %, precision 0.12

**Leak of SAM's raw segment** (3258 segments on scored pairs). Classes: clean (mostly o, precision ≥ 0.75), spill (mostly o, precision < 0.75), larger object (mostly another object but containing ≥ 50 % of o), different object.

| Variant | Population | Clean | Spill | Larger object | Different object |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pts | all segments | 0.714 | 0.092 | 0.057 | 0.137 |
| pts | under-cover | 0.305 | 0.156 | 0.062 | 0.477 |
| pts_whole | all segments | 0.399 | 0.129 | 0.258 | 0.213 |

- For pts, the clean share ranges from 0.584 to 0.789 as the precision threshold goes from 0.9 to 0.5. The segment's dominant label is not o in 19.4 % of all segments and 53.9 % of under-cover ones.
- 131 segments fall on objects that are absent from the target GT (10.4 Mpx).
- On the under-cover pairs, pts_whole segments are a median 10.2 × the object's GT size.

**Other variants** (registered config, all pairs; under-cover 140):
- pts_whole −0.00523 [−0.00787, −0.00250]; +0.00439
- pts_neg −0.00060 [−0.00099, −0.00020]; +0.00040
- box −0.00115 [−0.00192, −0.00038]; +0.00176
- mask_box −0.00094 [−0.00189, −0.00017]; +0.00077

Box-bounded prompts essentially cannot reach the outside class: outside recovery 0.0002 (box) and 0.0001 (mask_box).

**Sensitivity, reported only as ranges.** For pts over MIN_PROJ_PX {20, 200, 2000} and predicted-IoU gate {none, 0.7, 0.85}:
- all-pairs ΔJ&F [−0.00122, +0.00032]
- under-cover ΔJ&F [+0.00028, +0.00557]
- added-pixel precision [0.327, 0.595]

Either constant removes the billboard, whose projection is about 1,500 px and whose predicted IoU is 0.32–0.62.

**Why it fails, from the visual checks.** The part c_ini cannot see is usually a different visual segment from the part it can:

measures.summary:
I built candidate D (multi-view geometric-continuity growth) and measured it on the DEV set only: 85 non-keyframe frames, 3300 pairs, the 140-pair dev under-cover population and its 67-pair clean subset. No keyframe was read, scored or used for tuning; the scripts assert t != ref_frame. Everything ran on the host CPU with numpy/cv2; there was no GPU job and no tracked file changed (git status is the same as at the start).

**What I ran.** The design and every constant were written down in REGISTRATION.txt before any growth or score was computed. The only data looked at beforehand were GT-free Pi3 statistics.
- **Growth:** in every rig camera at frame t (21.7 cameras per frame on average), take the pixels that c_ini cannot see, that have valid depth, are not on a depth discontinuity, and whose colour passes a gate. The colour gate is learned from c_ini's own input mask (object vs rest, likelihood ratio ≥ 1). Join them into 4-connected components, link components across the 4 nearest cameras through depth-consistent correspondences, and keep every component reachable from a seed. A seed is a pixel that lands on c_ini's eroded mask of the object.
- **Projection into the target:** the target's own grown pixels, plus a nearest-point splat from all other cameras into target pixels that have no depth.
- **Composition:** add-only, the same rule as candidate C.
- **Variants:** mv (multi-view + splat, the declared primary), mv_nosplat, tv (target camera only), mv_noapp (no colour gate) and mv_plane (planar continuation for objects detected planar without GT).
- **Checks:** the pair set and baseline J and F match dev_pairs.json exactly, as do the visibility-class counts on all 3300 pairs.

**Result: candidate D does not help.**
- **Primary (mv):** J&F changes by −0.00476 on all pairs [−0.00780, −0.00223] and by −0.00235 on the under-cover pairs [−0.00793, +0.00219]. Only 27.0% of added pixels belong to the object (33.9% on under-cover pairs). It recovers 4.75% of the under-cover missed pixels.
- **Every variant and every constant setting tested** has an all-pair interval entirely below zero. The one exception is mv_noapp: it is about zero, but only because its huge, imprecise regions (precision 0.059) collide with each other and are thrown out as contested.
- **No setting improves the under-cover pairs reliably:** every interval includes zero.

**Why it fails.**
- **Leaks into objects the reference input does not contain.** Pixels c_ini cannot see include surfaces of objects outside the scored object set. Of the candidate pixels left after removing everything the existing masks already claim, 43.9% belong to such objects and 49.0% to other seeded objects whose masks do not claim them. Ground, wall and table growth floods furniture, painted props and counter items.
- **It cannot reach the costliest objects.**
  - FlameSteak cam01 wall: the colour gate separates its outside-view part from the seeds. Loosening the gate connects it but floods (4.9 M pixels added at precision 0.23).
  - CBA v06 grandstand: no target pixel projects onto c_ini's grandstand, and the sections are physically separate, so there is no seed and no chain.
  - Dog tree: 89% of its missed pixels have no depth, and the splat source is rarely grown.
- **Multi-view linking adds leaks, not reach.** Away from the Dog tree it recovers no more than growing in the target camera alone.

implications: Candidate D should not be registered for the keyframe. At the registered constants and all 12 one-at-a-time changes, every all-pair interval lies entirely below zero. No setting gives an under-cover gain distinguishable from zero.

The main failure is a protocol-structural leak. The region c_ini cannot see contains surfaces of objects outside the reference input: complete-only objects make up 0.439 of the unclaimed candidate pixels. Another 0.490 belong to seeded objects whose dev masks do not claim them. Geometry plus colour cannot separate these, because of contact surfaces (ground under furniture, wall behind props painted the wall's colour in AlexaMeadeFacePaint) and smooth Pi3 depth at object edges. The 'unclaimed by other D' rule only protects pixels some D already claims.

The costliest under-cover objects are out of reach of geometric continuity by construction. The CBA grandstand sections are physically disjoint, so there is no seed and no chain. The FlameSteak wall's outside-view part is separated by a colour change; a looser gate connects it but floods (precision 0.23). The Dog tree is mostly without depth, and its Pi3 is degenerate. This matches the protocol inventory: geometry carries no object identity into those pixels.

Multi-view linking adds leaks, not reach. Away from the Dog tree, target-only growth (tv) recovers as much (0.0523 vs 0.0510) at more than twice the raw precision (0.523 vs 0.197). The no-depth splat helps only the Dog tree, and even there it loses J&F (−0.022).

Recovery and precision trade off and never net positive. Recovery of the under-cover missed pixels ranges 0.043–0.228 across constants, but the best recovery comes at precision 0.239 and the best all-pair setting (LR 2) still loses 0.0013. A precision gate or limiting growth to particular object types would be a new design; it would need its own dev registration before any keyframe use.

The near-zero all-pair result of the geometry-only variant (+0.0004) is an artefact. Its huge regions (raw precision 0.059) overlap each other and are dropped as contested; it is not evidence that geometry alone is safe.

Planar continuation is the only sub-variant with positive clean-subset estimates (+0.0007 to +0.0101 across EPS_PLANE), but every interval includes zero and its all-pair change stays negative. At most it is a weak hint for wall/ground objects, not a basis for adoption.

Candidate E1 (text-concept) is a PROTOCOL CHANGE and diagnostic only. At test time it needs each object's class name from the annotation metadata (stage1/Data/<scene>/objects_labels.json, the same file as Data/MVSeg/<scene>/Mask/objects_labels.json). MUVOD's input is only c_ini's frame-0 mask, so the class name is not part of it. Two post-hoc arms also use the metadata field 'type'. Every number below is from the DEV set: 85 non-keyframe frames × 2 non-reference annotated cameras = 3300 pairs. No keyframe was read, prompted or scored (t != ref_frame is asserted in every script), and no tracked file was changed (git status is the same as at the start).

**Design.** I registered it before any detection was computed (REGISTRATION.txt):
- **Prompts.** Each seeded basic object's label is turned into SAM 3 text prompts. Primary rule: split '_or_' names into separate prompts, replace '_' with a space, drop a leading 'other '. Detections come from Sam3Processor(model.detector).set_image, then set_text_prompt, once per distinct prompt string per view, kept when prob > TAU (0.5).
- **Selection.**
  - V1 best_ov (primary): the detection with the largest overlap with P_o, the reprojected c_ini GT.
  - V2 best_iou: the detection with the highest IoU against P_o.
  - V3 union_maj: the union of detections whose c_ini-visible part mostly projects from o.
  - V4 union_all: every detection of the name, with no reference selection.
  - Diagnostic only: an oracle that picks the detection with the best IoU against the target GT.
- **Composition.** Add-only and identical to candidate C: add only pixels that c_ini cannot see, not claimed by any adopted geoset_rep_x dev mask, 8-connected to D_o, and not contested by another object.
- **Reused inputs.** P_o and the visibility classes come from candidate C's props.

**Registered result: effectively null.**
- **Primary on the 140 dev under-cover pairs (UC140):** +0.00052 J&F [-0.00028, +0.00151]. It recovers 0.11 % of their missed pixels.
- **Primary on all 3300 pairs:** +0.00029 [+0.00000, +0.00061].
- **Best registered variant, union_all:** UC140 +0.00676 [+0.00148, +0.01311], recovering 4.3 % of missed pixels, but all pairs -0.00025 [-0.00113, +0.00073].

**Why it fails.** The detector can see the region; the registered pipeline throws it away.
- The union of all detections of the name covers 50.7 % of the UC140 missed pixels, and 75.7 % of the missed pixels that have no Pi3 depth.
- Two registered steps throw this away:
  1. Selecting by overlap with the projection picks the instance c_ini already sees. The new extent sits in *other* detections. Example: Dog camera_0004's overhanging branches are a separate 'tree' detection (prob 0.87) with zero overlap with the projection.
  2. C's 8-connectivity rule cuts union_all's reach from 0.481 to 0.046 of missed pixels.

**Post-hoc check (not registered, written after seeing the results).** I removed the connectivity step and prompted only objects whose metadata type is 'env':
- **Dev results:** UC140 +0.00889 [+0.00001, +0.02334] (16 pairs up, 0 down); all pairs +0.00078 [+0.00001, +0.00215]; added-pixel precision 0.889.
- **Where the gain comes from:** almost entirely 2 of 49 under-cover objects:
  - the Dog tree: +0.173 per pair, recovering 72.5 % of its missed pixels at 0.987 precision;
  - FlameSteak cam01's wall: +0.072 per pair.
- **Without the env restriction:** removing connectivity for all objects is harmful (all pairs -0.00251), because names also match unseeded objects of the same class.

**Out of reach for text.** Several under-cover concepts get no detection at prob 0.3 or above on any of their dev views (5 frames each): 'grandstand' (CBABasketball v06 and v24), 'billboard' / 'bulletin board', 'rig' (MartialArts v13), 'floor' (Breakfast v9), 'fire' (Welder camera_0003) and 'cushion' / 'carpet' (CoffeeMartini cam10).

implications: The registered text-concept candidate is a null result and weaker than candidate C. The primary moves the 140 under-cover pairs by +0.0005 J&F and recovers 0.1 % of their missed pixels. Nothing in the registered set is worth carrying further, and it needs the class name at test time, which MUVOD does not provide.

The detector is not the bottleneck on the objects it can name: its union covers 51 % of the under-cover missed pixels and 76 % of the no-depth ones. The losses come from two parts of the registered pipeline. Selecting by overlap with the projection picks the instance c_ini already sees (the useful extent is a different detection), and candidate C's 8-connectivity rule cuts the reach from 0.48 to 0.05. The same connectivity rule probably limits candidate C and D's pipeline too, wherever the missing part is a disconnected region (the Dog tree's branches, FlameSteak's left wall).

Post hoc only: dropping connectivity and prompting only metadata-type 'env' objects gives dev UC140 +0.0089 and all pairs +0.0008, with 16 up / 0 down. But both CIs barely clear 0, and the gain is essentially two objects (Dog tree, FlameSteak cam01 wall), 10 of 140 pairs. Treat it as a hypothesis for a separately pre-registered follow-up on fresh dev frames, not as a result. It uses two metadata fields (name and type) that are outside MUVOD's input.

Without the env restriction, text additions are harmful: added-pixel precision is 0.01 for static and 0.15 for dynamic objects. Names also match unseeded or unlabelled objects of the same class (FlameSteak chair, Welder tool and metal part). Being unique within the scene's basic set does not make a name unique in the image.

Text cannot reach several of the costly under-cover objects at all. 'grandstand', 'billboard', 'rig', 'floor' (Breakfast), 'fire' and 'cushion/carpet' give no detection at prob 0.3 or above. Both CBABasketball grandstands and the billboard stay unsolved under any composition rule.

For a protocol-(i)-legal version (cross-image exemplar instead of the label), the lesson carries over. A proposal must be allowed to add instances that do not overlap the reference projection and are not connected to the current seed, and it then needs a precision guard; the env type served as that guard here.
All of this is dev-only, and the dev pairs are near-replicates (5 frames within 20 of the keyframe, the same objects). The post-hoc gains rest on 2 objects. No keyframe J&F was computed.

**This changes the task: stage 1 gets two annotated input views instead of one.** MUVOD gives stage 1 only c_ini's mask. Here each DEV target X (one of the 2 annotated non-reference cameras) also gets the GT of the other annotated non-reference camera B, from the same frame t, as a second reference. Under a real two-reference protocol B would be an input, not a scoring camera, so J&F³ itself would change. In these numbers each camera is scored only when the other one is the input. Treat everything below as a diagnostic upper bound, not a main-track candidate. Only DEV frames were decoded or scored (85 frames, 3300 pairs from the dev-route). No keyframe was read, and no tracked file changed; git status is the same as at the start.

**What I ran.** I did the full decode, not just the coverage measure. `dev_decode_2ref.py` rebuilds `decode_scene`'s path for the adopted preset `geoset_rep_x` for one target X:
- arm `geoset_pred_ft` with its own-fold checkpoint and leak guard;
- gate `reproj`, `--xcl out`, round 2 from predictions.

B's view is `wrapper.encode_reference(B image, B backbone, B GT of the c_ini objects, B's Pi3 grid in c_ini's frame)`, the GeoProj proj_bin / geoset_ft GT-memory path. Its confidence is "object present in B's GT", so an object B does not see adds nothing from B. The reproj gate still compares against c_ini's GT. All of this was fixed before any run. Three modes:
- **none** (control): no B.
- **both** (the two-reference protocol): references {c_ini, B} in round 1 for X and its candidates, and in round 2. The round-2 candidates are X's 3 nearest cameras minus {c_ini, B}.
- **r2**: B is added in round 2 only.

**The control matches.** Mode none reproduces the adopted dev masks byte for byte on 34/34 targets (first dev frame of each of the 17 scenes × 2 cameras).

**Overall result (mode both).**
- All 3300 dev pairs: J&F 0.9078 → 0.9145 (+0.0067).
- Dev under-cover population (140 pairs, fixed on the adopted decode): 0.5414 → 0.6486 (+0.1073). 111 of the 140 pairs are still below 0.8.
- Clean under-cover (precision ≥ 0.85, 67 pairs, the actual under-coverage case): only +0.0346, and +0.0257 without the Dog camera_0004 tree.

**Most of the under-cover gain is not about extent.** 62% of the summed gain comes from 4 Welder helmet/box groups. Those are miss and wrong-object pairs, where B's GT fixes which object is meant. Without those 4 groups the under-cover gain is +0.0447.

**The biggest misses barely move.**

| Object | J&F (adopted → both) | Missed pixels |
|---|---|---|
| FlameSteak cam01 wall | 0.732 → 0.797 (gain comes from fewer false-positive pixels) | 1.413M → 1.412M (unchanged) |
| CBABasketball v24 grandstand | 0.360 → 0.357 | — |
| CBABasketball v06 grandstand | 0.436 → 0.557 | — |
| Dog camera_0004 tree | 0.670 → 0.815 | 2.64M → 0.80M |

Across the 140 pairs the net drop in missed pixels is 5.55M → 3.32M (−40%). Most of that is the Dog tree: without it the drop is only −13%.

**Geometric reach of B is small.** Projecting the adopted decode's missed under-cover pixels from X into B:
- 0.071 of them are visible from B and 0.035 land on B's GT (pixel-weighted); 0.050 land on B's GT or c_ini's GT.
- By c_ini class: outside 0.029, occluded 0.128, no-depth 0 (by construction).
- In 20 of the 140 pairs, B's GT does not contain the object at all.

Mode both still recovers 0.424 of those missed pixels gross, but only 4.6% of what it recovers lies on B's projected GT (19.9% without the Dog tree). So the gain comes mostly from the B view in memory attention, not from labels carried over by reprojection.

**Round 1 matters.** The Dog tree, whose pixels mostly have no Pi3 depth, improves only when B is in round 1: clean pairs dominated by no-depth pixels gain +0.121 with both, −0.008 with r2. Mode r2 overall: all pairs +0.0056, under-cover +0.0921, clean +0.0119.

implications: This changes the task. A two-reference protocol makes B an input, so B could no longer be scored and J&F³ would change. These numbers score each annotated non-reference camera only when the other one is the second reference. They are a dev diagnostic and upper bound, not a main-track candidate, and no keyframe J&F was computed.

Even a perfect second annotated view from the same instant is a weak fix for real under-coverage. Clean under-cover pairs gain +0.035 J&F (+0.026 without the Dog tree), and 57 of the 67 stay below 0.8.

The large +0.107 on the full under-cover population is mostly a different failure. 62% of it is the Welder helmet and box miss/wrong-object pairs, where B's GT fixes which object is meant. That is not extent.

The outside class, which is the keyframe's main failure, barely moves. The FlameSteak wall's missed pixels are unchanged and the CBABasketball v24 grandstand stays at 0.36. A neighbouring annotated camera in this rig rarely sees what c_ini cannot: on DEV only 2.9% of the outside missed pixels land on B's GT. This matches protocol-inventory's 0.078 reach for the same 22 objects.

What gain there is comes mostly from B's view in memory attention, not from labels carried over by reprojection. Only 4.6% of the recovered under-cover pixels lie on B's projected GT. The Dog-tree no-depth pixels (no Pi3 depth, 0 geometric reach) recover only when B is in round 1 (+0.121 vs −0.008 with B in round 2 only). So a reference that is closer in appearance to the target can reach no-depth regions without geometry.

Recommendation: do not pursue a second-reference protocol change for the under-cover block. Its ceiling is low and it changes what is scored. Separately, the Welder identity fix and the round-1 effect on the Dog tree suggest the reference's appearance memory, not geometric reach, is what carries information beyond c_ini. Any protocol-legal source of a second view's labels should therefore enter round 1.

Caveat: dev pairs are near-replicates (5 frames, 49 under-cover objects). The cluster CIs are wide (under-cover scene CI [+0.026, +0.246]), and the gains say something about the same scenes, not an independent test.
